subject: Hosting pathway confirmation & PoC mandate — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting pathway confirmation & PoC mandate — next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to:  

Recap (call highlights)
- Primary requirement: PHI + state residency constraints for patient summaries and billing notes.
- Desired outcome: 6-week proof-of-concept to validate latency, privacy controls, and integration with Delta EMR.
- Traffic profile: initially ~100 requests/minute, peak 300 rpm for short windows.

Redwood recommendation (based on requirements)
- Private VPC (preferred): meets PHI and network isolation needs; recommended if procurement timeline allows.
- Dedicated capacity (fallback): reserved GPU pool in Redwood cloud for predictable throughput; can be stood up faster while VPC is provisioned.

Proposed PoC scope (what Redwood will deliver)
1) Kickoff + network onboarding (VPC peering/VPN) — 1 week
2) Integration + baseline tests (EMR connector, auth) — 2 weeks
3) Performance tuning (throughput, batching, KV cache) — 2 weeks
4) Acceptance and handover (SLA targets & runbook) — 1 week

Success criteria (we need confirmation from you)
- Average tail latency under 250ms at baseline profile (100 rpm).
- End-to-end data flow validated through your security sample file set.
- No PHI egress outside your VPC; key management confirmation.

Asks from Delta Health (please confirm)
- Final hosting choice: Private VPC or Dedicated as fallback
- Stakeholder contact for networking (name/email) and procurement owner
- Any additional compliance docs required for SOC2/HIPAA review

Attachments: PoC_Scope_Template.pdf, Security_QA.xlsx (see attached stubs)

Next steps
- If Private VPC chosen: we will provide a network checklist and a draft timeline (I’ll attach that once you confirm).
- If Dedicated chosen: we can provision reserved capacity in ~7 business days and start integration immediately.

Can you confirm hosting preference and procurement contact by EOD Wednesday so we can lock timelines?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Ben — great summary. A few clarifications from our side:  

1) Hosting preference: Private VPC. Delta Health will not accept any external-hosted PHI processing without VPC/network isolation and our key control.
2) Timeline constraints: procurement window for network approvals is ~4–6 weeks; security review can start immediately if you share your SOC2 and HIPAA attestation docs.
3) Throughput: initial 100 rpm is correct; we will provide a 2-hour peak-loading trace next week.
4) Stakeholders: Adam Lowe (IT networking) will own network onboarding; I’m the product owner for the PoC.

Adam’s contact: Adam Lowe <adam.lowe@deltahealth.com> — please loop him into the network checklist.

We’d like Redwood to propose both: (A) a Private VPC timeline and required inputs, and (B) a Dedicated-capacity fallback plan with expected costs and lead times, so execs can decide whether to accept a temporary Dedicated setup while VPC is provisioned.

Attaching a NOTE: our procurement team prefers receiving SOW+detailed timeline prior to contract routing.

Best,
Elena
Director, Product — Delta Health
elena@deltahealth.com

Elena / Adam — thanks for the quick confirmation. Based on your preference for Private VPC, below is the concrete PoC plan I’ll share with procurement and IT. Please review and flag any gaps.

Proposed PoC plan (Private VPC primary, Dedicated fallback)
- Week 0 (Planning): SOW, NDA updates, sign PoC order form. Provide SOC2 + HIPAA docs.
- Week 1 (Network onboarding): Exchange IP CIDR, VPN setup or VPC peering; test connectivity to a non-PHI sandbox.
- Weeks 2–3 (Integration): EMR connector development, auth flows (OIDC/SAML), baseline correctness tests with 50 sample patient records.
- Weeks 4–5 (Performance run): Load testing to simulate 100 -> 300 rpm peaks; batching/quantization tuning; observability dashboard shared with Delta.
- Week 6 (Acceptance): Run acceptance suite, transfer runbooks, optional canary traffic.

Acceptance criteria (refined)
- Functional: 98% successful end-to-end responses on the sample set.
- Performance: 95th pct latency < 400ms during peak, average < 250ms at baseline.
- Security: Network traffic limited to Delta CIDRs; keys managed via your KMS or HSM (we will support Bring Your Own Key).

Fallback: If procurement cannot complete within 3 weeks, Redwood can provision Dedicated capacity to run integration and baseline tests. Dedicated cost/lead-time will be in the SOW (I’ll attach numbers).

Owners / stakeholders
- Delta: Elena Park (Product), Adam Lowe (Networking), Procurement TBD
- Redwood: Ben Carter (PoC lead), Karthik Iyer (Solutions Architect), Marissa Cole (CS/Onboarding)

I’ve attached a tentative timeline spreadsheet (redwood_poc_timeline.xlsx) and the PoC_Scope_Template.pdf. If this looks good I’ll convert the plan into a short SOW and pricing for Delta procurement.

Next actions
1) Adam: can you share the networking contact and preferred window for a 30-minute network kickoff?
2) Elena: confirm procurement owner so we can route SOW.
3) Redwood: will prepare two SOW variants (Private VPC and Dedicated fallback) by COB Thursday.

Ben

All — I reviewed Ben’s proposed plan. A few practical notes from onboarding/CS perspective:  

1) Private VPC provisioning is the safest for PHI but often takes longer (network approvals + customer security checklist).
2) Dedicated as a fallback is sensible — call out clearly in the SOW which parts migrate later to VPC and who owns data deletion/transfer responsibilities. Pricing for Dedicated short-term use is higher per-token but avoids a multi-week hold.
3) Add a separate risk register section in the SOW listing: firewall rules, certificate rotation, KMS handoff, and rollback plan.

I’ll help draft the SOW language for migration and the risk register. Ben — I can join the network kickoff if it helps with technical handoffs.

Marissa Cole
